title: the DSG movement chapter part II - the bridges, the expanded falling rules, spelunking, excavation, fatigue, darkness and slippery surfaces

banner.title: The DSG MOVEMENT CHAPTER PART II, R505: the printed pp. 19-22 (pdf 20-23) second half of the movement chapter - the bridge rules (the maintained no-check rule, the suspension/wooden/stone permanent bridges, the rope and log impromptu bridges with the move-log ladder), the expanded falling rules (the cumulative 1d6-per-10-feet dice, the 20d6 and 10d6 caps, the 50-foot stop window, the landing ladder, the slope slides), spelunking with TABLE 7 MINIMUM PASSAGEWAY SIZES, the excavation with TABLE 8 ARMOR EFFECTS ON CHARACTER WIDTH, the fatigue and exhaustion ladders, the darkness movement with TABLE 9 COURSE CHANGES IN DARKNESS, and the slippery horizontal surfaces with the crampon rules. The movement chapter parent closes this round: the whole chapter is pinned.
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (the user own copy), printed pp. 19-22 = pdf 20-23, pulled per-page on the r504-extraction branch (p020-p023) with the tsv confidence tables and the 300-dpi page images under extract/r504/ on main; the Table 7 human/dwarf/half-orc rows and the Table 8 splint/banded/plate/field cells were image-only reads, each cross-checked against the tsv fragments (the residual cautions live in the r504 extraction grids file).
banner.sentinel: THE SETTLE: census 429 -> 430; the gap report 27/128 -> 38 closed / 117 open (the seven movement-chapter boxes from bridges through slippery surfaces, the movement parent, and the manifest tables 7-9; the movement chapter is now fully closed). CROSS-BOOK SEAM: the fall dice ladder, the 20d6 cap and the 50-foot stop window verified const-for-const against rules/wsgfall.h and rules/wsgstop.h (agreement at every compared value); the slippery rules against rules/wsgslip.h and the waterfall against the WSG water pins (no divergence; the 10d6 waterfall cap is DSG-only, the WSG has no cap pin); the fatigue against rules/wsgfatig.h (const-for-const agreement on the 4/2 cycle, the 6-then-5-then-shrinking check interval, the -2 effects, the 12-turn clear and the 6-turn recoveries - ONE FRAMING DIVERGENCE: the WSG exhausted penalty is an additional -2, the DSG a -4 instead of the fatigue -2; both total -4 and the DSG pins as printed). NOTHING auto-credited.

audit_comment: The DSG movement chapter part II pins the bridge rules (the maintained no-check rule; the suspension 25-percent-per-character give-way with the one-hand catch at -25; the anchor sabotage 1d8 rounds detectable only by a thief; the sawed rope one round and visible; the wooden 5-percent-per-year rot with the 1d20+20-year beams and the 50-percent rotten step; the stone impervious, the arch collapse 1d4 rounds and the instant foundation collapse; the rope bridge +50 with the -20 sabotaged cling; the log bridge +40, +20 sloped, +80 crawling, with the move-log ladder), the expanded falling rules (the cumulative dice with the 6d6-at-30 example, the 20d6 and 10d6 caps, the 1,000-feet-per-round rate, the 50-foot stop window, the landing ladder, the slope slide), spelunking (the 2/3 ceiling, the hands-and-knees and prone penalties, Table 7), excavation (the rubble and solid-barrier rates, Table 8), fatigue and exhaustion (the 4/2 cycle, the shrinking check interval, the -2 and -4 effects, the recoveries), the darkness movement (the rates, the secret d12 course roll, Table 9), and the slippery surfaces (the dex checks, the melee fall penalties, the crampons).

consts.name: dmxSuspensionGiveWayPct
consts.comment: an old suspension bridge stands a 25 percent chance per character crossing it of giving way at some crucial point.

consts.name: dmxSuspensionCatchBridgeModPct
consts.comment: a character who fails the first suspension check and tries to catch a piece of the bridge with only one hand free checks at -25 percent; he can drop what he is holding to free both hands.

consts.name: dmxAnchorSabotageDie
consts.comment: sabotaging an anchor point of a suspension bridge takes 1d8 rounds.

consts.name: dmxSawRopeRounds
consts.comment: sawing through a rope support of a suspension bridge can be done in one round.

consts.name: dmxWoodRotPctPerYear
consts.comment: a wooden bridge not inspected and repaired within the past year stands a 5 percent chance per year of sustaining rot.

consts.name: dmxWoodBeamDie
consts.comment: the actual supporting beams of a wooden bridge last 1d20+20 years before beginning to rot; rot first affects the planks and railings.

consts.name: dmxWoodBeamBaseYears
consts.comment: the beam-rot base: 1d20 plus 20 years.

consts.name: dmxRottenStepPct
consts.comment: each character crossing a rotted wooden bridge stands a 50 percent chance of stepping onto a rotten portion.

consts.name: dmxArchCenterCollapseDie
consts.comment: if the center of a stone bridge arch is destroyed (transmute rock to mud), the entire bridge collapses in 1d4 rounds.

consts.name: dmxRopeBridgeModPct
consts.comment: a character crossing a rope bridge (one rope for the feet, one for the hands) makes a Climbing Check with a +50 percent modifier.

consts.name: dmxRopeSabotageClingModPct
consts.comment: a character clinging to the sabotaged rope with his hands checks at -20 percent, or may elect to hold on and swing down with it.

consts.name: dmxLogDiaHeightDiv
consts.comment: a log bridge must be 1/4 or less of the character height in diameter to require a check; wider log bridges are crossed automatically.

consts.name: dmxLogBridgeModPct
consts.comment: crossing a log bridge requires a Climbing Check with a +40 percent modifier.

consts.name: dmxLogSlopedModPct
consts.comment: if the log bridge slopes upward or downward, the modifier drops to +20 percent.

consts.name: dmxLogCrawlModPct
consts.comment: if the character crawls or has both hands free, the log bridge modifier is +80 percent.

consts.name: dmxHumanLogFt
consts.comment: the move-log ladder floor: a normal human can move a log of 10 feet or shorter length (a 1 1/2-foot diameter log).

consts.name: dmxStr17LogFt
consts.comment: a human with 17 or 18 Strength, or a creature like an ogre, can move a 20-foot log.

consts.name: dmxHillGiantLogFt
consts.comment: a hill giant, or a fairly young dragon, can move a 30-foot log.

consts.name: dmxLargeGiantLogLoFt
consts.comment: a large giant or dragon can move a 40-foot log.

consts.name: dmxLargeGiantLogHiFt
consts.comment: a large giant or dragon can move a log of up to 50 feet in length.

consts.name: dmxFallIncrementPer10Ft
consts.comment: falling damage is 1d6 for the first 10 feet, 2d6 for the second, 3d6 for the third, and so on - each 10-foot band adds one more die, cumulative.

consts.name: dmxThirtyFtFallDice
consts.comment: the printed example: a 30-foot fall inflicts a total of 6d6 (1+2+3).

consts.name: dmxFallCapDice
consts.comment: the maximum damage any fall can inflict is 20d6, regardless of the height.

consts.name: dmxWaterfallCapDice
consts.comment: the maximum damage a character can sustain by falling over a waterfall is 10d6.

consts.name: dmxFallFtPerRound
consts.comment: for purposes of game balance, a character falls 1,000 feet in one round unless the fall is interrupted.

consts.name: dmxStopWindowFt
consts.comment: an attempt to slow a fall by catching onto a wall or climbing surface can only be made in the first 50 feet - past that the momentum is too great.

consts.name: dmxStopNonslipDiv
consts.comment: on a nonslippery climbing surface the fall is stopped on a d100 roll less than or equal to 1/2 the Climbing Rating.

consts.name: dmxStopSlightDiv
consts.comment: a slightly slippery surface can be caught on 1/4 the Climbing Rating - half the nonslippery chance.

consts.name: dmxRoughLandingMult
consts.comment: a landing on broken rocks, debris, or a slanted surface that ricochets the character inflicts double the normal fall damage.

consts.name: dmxSpikeDamageDie
consts.comment: each spike or weapon-like feature of a landing area inflicts an extra d6 of damage beyond the fall.

consts.name: dmxSparseSpikeMinDice
consts.comment: a 1d6 grouping of spikes means the character impales himself on 1 to 6 of them.

consts.name: dmxSparseSpikeMaxDice
consts.comment: the sparse spike grouping impales on up to 6 spikes.

consts.name: dmxDenseSpikeMinDice
consts.comment: a 3d6 grouping of densely packed spikes impales on 3 to 18 spikes.

consts.name: dmxDenseSpikeMaxDice
consts.comment: the dense spike grouping impales on up to 18 spikes, 3-18 d6 of damage in addition to the fall.

consts.name: dmxSoftLandingDiv
consts.comment: a soft landing on sand, mud, soft loam, pine branches or flesh inflicts only half the normal fall damage.

consts.name: dmxVerySoftFailDiv
consts.comment: a failed very-soft save still halves the fall damage.

consts.name: dmxWaterLandingDiePer100Ft
consts.comment: a successful Dexterity Check into water costs 1d6 of damage for every 100 feet of the fall.

consts.name: dmxExample250FtWaterDice
consts.comment: the printed example: a character falling 250 feet into water with a successful Dexterity Check suffers only 3d6.

consts.name: dmxSlideFreeFt
consts.comment: a character sliding down a sloping surface suffers no damage in the first 20 feet of the slide.

consts.name: dmxSlideDiePer10Ft
consts.comment: past the first 20 feet, a slide inflicts 1d6 of damage for each 10 feet of the slide (the abrasions), unless the slope is very slippery.

consts.name: dmxSlideLandingDiePer40Ft
consts.comment: the landing after a slide inflicts 1d6 for each 40 feet of the slide.

consts.name: dmxSlipperySlideLandingMult
consts.comment: a slide down a slippery slope takes double the normal damage upon landing.

consts.name: dmxUprightMinCeilNum
consts.comment: if the tunnel ceiling is lower than the character height but at least 2/3 of it, he can walk upright.

consts.name: dmxUprightMinCeilDen
consts.comment: the upright-walk ceiling floor is 2/3 the character height.

consts.name: dmxUprightRateNum
consts.comment: walking upright under a low ceiling moves at 2/3 of the normal movement rate, with no adverse combat effects.

consts.name: dmxUprightRateDen
consts.comment: the upright low-ceiling rate denominator: 2/3 normal.

consts.name: dmxHandsKneesRateDiv
consts.comment: a character traveling on hands and knees (a tunnel under 2/3 his height) moves at 1/2 his normal movement rate.

consts.name: dmxHandsKneesAtkMod
consts.comment: a character fighting on hands and knees suffers a -5 penalty to all his attack rolls.

consts.name: dmxProneCeilDiv
consts.comment: in a tunnel whose diameter is 1/4 or less of his height, the character must slither along prone.

consts.name: dmxProneRateDiv
consts.comment: a prone character is limited to 1/4 of his normal rate of movement.

consts.name: dmxProneAtkMod
consts.comment: a prone character suffers a -8 modifier to all his attack rolls.

consts.name: dmxRubbleClearFtDie
consts.comment: in one turn of excavation a character can clear 1d4 feet of loosely packed rubble passageway to the Table 7 minimum width.

consts.name: dmxRubblePartialDieMult
consts.comment: if the passage is only partially blocked, the distance cleared in a turn is 2d4 feet.

consts.name: dmxSolidRateDiv
consts.comment: if other metal tools (shovels, swords) are substituted for pickaxes, the excavation rate is only 1/4 the Table 27 rate.

consts.name: dmxPassagewayRowCount
consts.comment: Table 7 has six race rows: human, half-orc, dwarf, gnome, elf and halfling.

consts.name: dmxArmorWidthRowCount
consts.comment: Table 8 has eleven armor rows: leather, padded, studded leather, scale, ring, chain, splint, banded, plate, field plate and full plate.

consts.name: dmxCourseChangeRowCount
consts.comment: Table 9 has twelve d12 rows, 1 through 12.

consts.name: dmxT9RolledDirDie
consts.comment: the 135-degree row resolves its direction on 1d6.

consts.name: dmxT9RolledRightLo
consts.comment: on the 135-degree row, a 1-3 rolls the course to the right.

consts.name: dmxT9RolledRightHi
consts.comment: the right-direction ceiling on the rolled row: 1-3 of the 1d6.

consts.name: dmxFatigueWorkTurns
consts.comment: a character can avoid fatigue by resting for two turns after each four turns of unusually strenuous activity - keep the pattern and he is never susceptible.

consts.name: dmxFatigueRestTurns
consts.comment: the paired rest: two turns of rest per four turns of work.

consts.name: dmxFatigueFirstCheckTurns
consts.comment: six turns of unusually strenuous activity without the two turns of rest force a Constitution Check; failure fatigues the character.

consts.name: dmxFatigueSecondCheckAfterTurns
consts.comment: after a successful first check, five more turns of strenuous activity force another Constitution Check.

consts.name: dmxFatigueIntervalStepTurns
consts.comment: each subsequent successful check shortens the interval by one turn - five, then four, and so on until the character must check every turn.

consts.name: dmxFatigueRecoveryTurns
consts.comment: a character whose checks have all succeeded fully recovers by spending an hour (six turns) resting.

consts.name: dmxFatigueAttrMod
consts.comment: a fatigued character has all his attribute scores lowered by 2, with the attendant temporary losses of hit points, spells and combat bonuses.

consts.name: dmxFatigueCombatMod
consts.comment: a fatigued character applies a -2 penalty to all his attack rolls, damage rolls and saves.

consts.name: dmxFatigueEffectTurns
consts.comment: the fatigue effects last until the character rests for two hours (12 turns).

consts.name: dmxExhaustedMod
consts.comment: an exhausted character forced to act suffers a -4 penalty to all the attribute and combat scores affected by fatigue.

consts.name: dmxExhaustRecoveryTurns
consts.comment: after one hour of uninterrupted rest an exhausted character rolls a Constitution Check (revised score); success makes him merely fatigued, failure forces another full hour.

consts.name: dmxDarkSafeRateDiv
consts.comment: characters in the dark can safely move at 1/3 their normal movement rates, probing the ground ahead.

consts.name: dmxDarkCourseDie
consts.comment: the DM makes a secret roll on 1d12 for the unknown course changes that occur walking in complete darkness.

consts.name: dmxDarkCourseRollEveryTurns
consts.comment: the course roll is made after every three turns spent walking in darkness.

consts.name: dmxDarkCourseShortModPerTurn
consts.comment: if the uncharted movement lasted less than three turns, the roll is still made, with a -1 modifier to the d12 for each turn short.

consts.name: dmxDarkRoughFallDamage
consts.comment: each failed Dexterity Check on a rough or uneven floor means the character sustains 1 point of damage in a rough fall.

consts.name: dmxDarkRoughSafeRateDiv
consts.comment: characters traveling rough floors in darkness prevent the accidents by slowing to 1/6 their normal rate.

consts.name: dmxSlipRiseRounds
consts.comment: a character who falls on a slippery surface spends a full round climbing to his feet.

consts.name: dmxSlipSlowdownRounds
consts.comment: a character can spend a round slowing down from normal speed to 1/2 speed, and then turn without a check.

consts.name: dmxSlipFailAcPenalty
consts.comment: a character who fails the melee Dexterity Check on a slippery surface suffers a +4 penalty to his Armor Class for the round.

consts.name: dmxSlipFailRiseRounds
consts.comment: after a failed melee slip the character spends the next round getting to his feet, the AC penalty remaining in effect, and cannot attack that round.

consts.name: dmxSlipGroundAtkMod
consts.comment: a character who elects to fight from the ground keeps the +4 AC penalty and incurs a -4 penalty on all his attack rolls.

consts.name: dmxCramponAttachTurns
consts.comment: a pair of crampons requires one turn to attach.

consts.name: dmxCramponNoiseMult
consts.comment: a character walking on a nonslippery surface in crampons makes twice as much noise as he otherwise would.

consts.name: dmxCramponWearDie
consts.comment: walking on nonslippery surfaces wears the crampons out in 1d6 miles of such abuse.

bools.name: dmxMaintainedBridgeNoChecks
bools.comment: a bridge maintained periodically and not sabotaged is crossed without any checks, regardless of type.

bools.name: dmxSuspensionGiveWayPerChar
bools.comment: the suspension give-way chance is rolled per character crossing, not per crossing.

bools.name: dmxAnchorSabotageThiefDetectOnly
bools.comment: anchor sabotage can only be detected by a thief find traps roll.

bools.name: dmxSawRopeVisible
bools.comment: a sawed rope support is readily visible to any character who examines the bridge.

bools.name: dmxRottenStepSuspensionChecks
bools.comment: a character who steps onto a rotten portion makes Climbing Checks to determine whether he falls, as described for suspension bridges.

bools.name: dmxStoneBridgeSabotageImmune
bools.comment: stone bridges are the most solid, virtually impervious to the effects of sabotage and age.

bools.name: dmxStoneWeightCollapseRare
bools.comment: even a weakened stone bridge will rarely collapse because of the added weight of a character.

bools.name: dmxFoundationCollapseInstant
bools.comment: if a stone bridge foundation is destroyed, the bridge collapses instantly.

bools.name: dmxFoundationCollapseToNext
bools.comment: a foundation collapse runs in both directions from the ruined foundation until it reaches the next foundation or the end of the bridge.

bools.name: dmxRopeBridgeArmorRaceApply
bools.comment: armor and race modifiers affect the rope bridge roll normally.

bools.name: dmxRopeSabotageUnmodifiedCheck
bools.comment: a character on a rope bridge when one rope is chopped through makes an unmodified Climbing Check or falls.

bools.name: dmxLogWiderAutoCross
bools.comment: a log bridge wider than 1/4 the character height is crossed without a check.

bools.name: dmxStopSlipperyImpossible
bools.comment: a slippery climbing surface cannot be used to stop a fall.

bools.name: dmxVerySoftSaveVsParalysis
bools.comment: a character making a very soft landing (a prepared cushion of feathers or straw) makes a saving throw vs. paralyzation.

bools.name: dmxWaterLandingRoundUp
bools.comment: the water-landing damage dice are rounded up: a 250-foot fall costs 3d6.

bools.name: dmxNoCatchAndWaterSameRound
bools.comment: a character cannot attempt to stop a fall by catching a climbing surface and make a Dexterity Check to land in water during the same round.

bools.name: dmxWaterCheckSecondRoundAllowed
bools.comment: if the fall lasts more than one round, the character can attempt the Dexterity Check on the second round.

bools.name: dmxSlipperySlideNoDamage
bools.comment: on a smooth and relatively slippery slope the character sustains no damage while sliding.

bools.name: dmxHandsKneesLoseDexShieldAc
bools.comment: a hands-and-knees character also loses all Dexterity and shield bonuses to AC.

bools.name: dmxHandsKneesLongWeaponsUnusable
bools.comment: weapons such as longbows, broadswords and battleaxes cannot be employed in these close quarters (the Space Required listing on the Weapons Tables is the guide).

bools.name: dmxProneNoShieldDexAc
bools.comment: a prone character can gain no Armor Class benefits from a shield or a Dexterity bonus.

bools.name: dmxProneWeaponLimitsWorse
bools.comment: the prone space limits his choice of weapons even further than the hands-and-knees position.

bools.name: dmxDragPackTighter
bools.comment: the passageway sizes assume no bulky armor or backpack - a character usually drags his pack behind him, negotiating tighter passages.

bools.name: dmxSolidPickaxesAssumed
bools.comment: the solid-barrier excavation rates assume the characters use pickaxes.

bools.name: dmxFatigueHenchmenStay
bools.comment: henchmen will not desert because of the temporary Charisma lowering.

bools.name: dmxFatigueContinuingCheckEveryTurn
bools.comment: a fatigued character who continues the strenuous activity must make a Constitution Check every turn.

bools.name: dmxFatigueCheckVsRevisedCon
bools.comment: the fatigued every-turn checks roll against his revised Constitution score.

bools.name: dmxFatigueMarchNotStrenuous
bools.comment: merely marching along, even over difficult terrain, is not an unusually strenuous activity; fighting, running, continuous climbing, chopping wood, rough or swift swimming, and moving while encumbered are.

bools.name: dmxExhaustedNoVoluntaryLabor
bools.comment: an exhausted character cannot perform any voluntary physical labor and must rest until he recovers.

bools.name: dmxExhaustedInsteadOfFatigue
bools.comment: the exhausted -4 is instead of, not in addition to, the fatigue penalties (a WSG divergence - the WSG frames exhaustion as an additional -2; both books total -4).

bools.name: dmxExhaustCheckToFatigued
bools.comment: a successful exhaustion-recovery check leaves the character fatigued, not fresh.

bools.name: dmxDarkObstacleDexCheck
bools.comment: a character moving at normal rates in darkness who encounters an obstacle must make a Dexterity Check or his momentum carries him into it.

bools.name: dmxDarkNeedDirectionMeans
bools.comment: without some means of determining direction, such as trailing a hand along a corridor wall, it is virtually impossible to walk a straight line in complete darkness.

bools.name: dmxSlipStraightLineSafe
bools.comment: characters cautiously treading a slippery surface can travel at their normal movement rate as long as they move in a straight line.

bools.name: dmxSlipTurnStopRunDexCheck
bools.comment: if the character attempts to turn, stop suddenly, or break into a run on a slippery surface, he must make a Dexterity Check or fall down.

bools.name: dmxSlipFallNoDamage
bools.comment: a character who falls down on a slippery surface suffers no damage.

bools.name: dmxSlipHalfRateTurnFree
bools.comment: a character moving at 1/2 his normal movement rate can turn without making a Dexterity Check.

bools.name: dmxSlipMeleeCheckEveryAttack
bools.comment: characters engaging in melee combat on a slippery surface must make a Dexterity Check before every attack; a failed check means no attack and a fall.

bools.name: dmxCramponsNeverFall
bools.comment: characters wearing crampons always retain their footing on slick surfaces - no Dexterity Checks are needed while turning or fighting.

bools.name: dmxCramponRemoveHalfTurn
bools.comment: crampons take half a turn to remove.

tables.name: Table 7: MINIMUM PASSAGEWAY SIZES
col_comments: The minimum tunnel width in inches by race row: human 24, half-orc 24, dwarf 24, gnome 18, elf 18, halfling 12 - the printed 2, 2, 2, 1 1/2, 1 1/2 and 1 feet.
The minimum tunnel crawl height in inches by race row: human 12, half-orc 16, dwarf 12, gnome 9, elf 9, halfling 8 - the printed 1, 1 1/3, 1, 3/4, 3/4 and 2/3 feet.
tables.audit_comment: the Table 7 grid: the six race rows x the tunnel-width and crawl-height columns, pinned in inches (the feet-and-fraction print converted at 12 inches the foot); the human, dwarf and half-orc rows were image-only reads cross-checked against the tsv fragments.

tables.name: Table 8: ARMOR EFFECTS ON CHARACTER WIDTH
col_comments: The increase in the character width in inches by armor row: leather 0, padded 2, studded leather 2, scale 3, ring 2, chain 3, splint 3, banded 6, plate 8, field plate 10, full plate 12 - the printed none, 1/6, 1/6, 1/4, 1/6, 1/4, 1/4, 1/2, 2/3, 5/6 and 1 foot.
tables.audit_comment: the Table 8 grid: the eleven armor rows x the width-increase column, pinned in inches; the splint, banded, plate and field-plate cells were image-only reads cross-checked against the tsv fragments.

tables.name: Table 9: COURSE CHANGES IN DARKNESS
col_comments: The course change in degrees by d12 row: rows 1-3 straight ahead (0), rows 4-5 forty-five right, rows 6-7 forty-five left, row 8 sixty right, row 9 sixty left, row 10 ninety right, row 11 ninety left, row 12 one hundred thirty-five.
The direction by d12 row: 0 straight, 1 right, 2 left, and 3 the 135-degree row whose direction rolls on 1d6 (1-3 right, 4-6 left).
tables.audit_comment: the Table 9 grid: the twelve d12 rows x the degrees and direction columns; rows 1-7 were image-only reads cross-checked against the tsv fragments.
